app.name: Photo
app.description: A browser-based photo culling and editing app, in the spirit of Lightroom. Users open a folder of photos, cull them (rate, flag, colour-label), make non-destructive edits, and export. Every operation is an action in a central registry; the keyboard, menus, command palette and AI all dispatch the same actions.

conventions: Every operation is an action, invoked by id with a JSON params object validated against the action's schema.
Read state with query actions (kind: query) before proposing changes; they have no side effects.
Respect each action's availability: dispatching an unavailable action fails.
Commands marked undoable are recorded in history. A plan of several steps is applied as one transaction, so one undo reverts it.
Library commands with an optional photoIds parameter act on the current selection when it is omitted.
Shortcut keys use `mod` for Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere; chords are space-separated strokes.
Photo ids are paths relative to the open folder, e.g. "2026-09/DSC_0001.jpg". Capture times are camera-local, formatted YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss without a time zone.
Culling commands accept advance: true to move to the next photo afterwards; when called by an AI or script they never auto-advance otherwise.

concepts.explanation: The set of photos currently loaded, in display order. Each photo has an id, file name, capture time, rating, flag and colour label. Image file contents are never modified.
One or more selected photos, plus one active photo (the one shown in Loupe and Develop). Library commands that accept an optional `photoIds` parameter act on the selection when it is omitted.
`pick`, `reject` or `none` (unflagged). Rejects are typically hidden or deleted later.
The on-screen library can be filtered (minimum rating, flags, labels, file name) and sorted. Navigation and Select All follow what is visible. Query actions can filter independently of the screen.

After a rating, flag or label command on a single photo, the app can move to the next photo: only while Caps Lock is on (default, as in Lightroom), always, or never. AI and scripts pass advance: true instead.

The library is one folder (with subfolders). Ratings, flags and labels are stored in the app and, when the folder was opened with write access, in XMP sidecars next to the photos so Lightroom, Bridge and darktable can read them. The contents of photos are never modified.

Camera RAW files (CR2, CR3, NEF, ARW, DNG, RAF, ORF, RW2 and others; mimeType image/x-…) are photos like any other: rated, edited and exported the same way. While RAW+JPEG grouping is on (the default; see library.pairs.set), a RAW and a JPEG with the same name are one photo: the RAW is listed and the JPEG is hidden and moves with it when it is removed. When it is off, they are two separate photos.

Metadata (rating, flags, EXIF, capture time) comes from query actions. To judge what is in a photo (sharpness, faces, subject, colour, how an edit looks), view it with library.photos.view, which returns images with the current edits applied. Viewing costs tokens: scan with thumbnails, check focus with detail.

Rejected photos can be removed from the library: they move, with their sidecars, into a _Rejected subfolder of the open folder and can be restored from there. Only emptying that folder deletes files, permanently (not to the system Trash), and it needs the user's explicit confirmation.
`grid` shows thumbnails for fast scanning, `loupe` shows the active photo large for close review, and `develop` shows the active photo with editing controls.

Non-destructive develop settings stored per photo as JSON: white balance (temperature, tint), exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, vibrance, saturation, a post-crop vignette, a tone curve, HSL per colour band, and crop/straighten, plus an optional profile. Rendered on the GPU; saved with the ratings and in the XMP sidecar. Exports apply them at full resolution. A photo with default settings is unedited.

A profile is a film look applied under the sliders (as in Lightroom): colour or black and white, per-channel curves, split toning, fade and grain, with an amount (0–200%). Applying one keeps the sliders. There are built-in profiles (ids `builtin.…`) and the user's own (`user.…`), which can be created, edited, deleted, and exported to or imported from JSON files. A photo's edit holds a copy of its profile's look, so it renders the same where that profile isn't installed.

`develop.auto` sets tone (exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, vibrance) and/or white balance from each photo's own pixels, inside its crop, accounting for its profile. Each photo is analysed separately, so a batch gets individual settings in one undo step.
Undoable commands are recorded in history. A transaction groups several commands into one undo step; AI-proposed plans are always applied as a single transaction after the user reviews them.

workflows.title: Reject the blurry frames in a burst
workflows.goal: Keep the sharpest of several near-identical photos.

steps.note: Find the burst by capture time.
Compare them; use detail size on the best candidates to check focus.
Reject the softer frames.
Pick the sharpest.

workflows.title: Give the selected photos a warm film look
workflows.goal: Warm, slightly faded, less saturated, as one undoable step.

steps.note: Applies to every selected photo.

workflows.title: Give a set of photos a consistent look
workflows.goal: Apply one film profile to the selection, then correct each photo's exposure and white balance individually.

steps.note: Choose a profile by its description (or the user's own).
Apply it to every selected photo.
Then Auto, so each photo is corrected under the profile.

workflows.title: Make a reusable profile
workflows.goal: Save a look as one of the user's own profiles and apply it.

steps.note: Start from a built-in look and change some fields; returns the new id.
Apply it with the returned id.
Optionally save it to a file to share.

workflows.title: Edit one photo, then match the rest
workflows.goal: Develop the active photo and copy its look to the other selected photos.

steps.note: Adjust the active photo (select just it first).
Select the photos to match.
Copies everything except crop from the active photo.

workflows.title: Cull a shoot
workflows.goal: Go through every photo once, picking keepers and rejecting the rest.

steps.note: Check what is loaded and which photo is active.
Review one photo at a time at a large size.
Pick the active photo and move on…
…or reject it and move on.
Afterwards, show only the picks.

workflows.title: Rate a batch of selected photos
workflows.goal: Give the current selection the same star rating in one undoable step.

steps.note: Confirm which photos are selected.
Rate them all; omit photoIds to use the selection.

workflows.title: Show only the best photos
workflows.goal: Find the photos rated 4 stars or more.

steps.note: Find them (ids, names, metadata).
Or show only them on screen.

workflows.title: Show this morning's best photos
workflows.goal: Find 4+ star photos captured before noon on a given day.

steps.note: Check the folder and the capture dates in view.
Capture times are camera-local.
Select the matches by id.

workflows.title: Warm up and brighten the selection
workflows.goal: Apply a warmer white balance and a little more exposure to every selected photo.

steps.note: Check which photos are selected.
Shift white balance warmer, relative to each photo.
Raise exposure by a third of a stop.

actions.title: List Actions
actions.description: Return every registered action's id, title, category, kind and whether it is available right now. Use availableOnly to see only what can run in the current context.

availableOnly.description: Only actions available in the current context.

actions.title: Toggle AI Panel
actions.description: Show or hide the AI conversation panel, which keeps every suggestion and what was applied.

actions.title: Close AI Settings
actions.description: Close the AI settings screen.
actions.availability: Available only when AI settings are open.

actions.title: AI Settings…
actions.description: Open AI settings: the Anthropic API key (stored only in this browser) and which Claude model plans requests.

actions.title: New AI Conversation
actions.description: Start a new AI conversation for this folder. The previous conversation and its suggestions are discarded.
actions.availability: Available only when there is an AI conversation.

actions.title: Set Auto-Advance
actions.description: Choose when rating, flagging or labelling a photo moves on to the next one: capsLock (only while Caps Lock is on, as in Lightroom; the default), always, or never. Applies to keyboard, palette, menu and button use; AI and scripts advance only when they pass advance: true. The choice is remembered.

examples.description: Always move to the next photo after culling.
Lightroom behaviour: only while Caps Lock is on.

actions.title: Get App Context
actions.description: Return a summary of the current app state: view, theme, library size, selection, active photo and undo/redo availability. Call this first to understand what the user is looking at.

actions.title: Close Context Menu
actions.description: Close the open context menu without running anything.
actions.availability: Available only when a context menu is open.

actions.title: Open Context Menu
actions.description: Open a context menu. Without menuId, opens the photo menu for the current view next to the active photo (the keyboard equivalent of right-clicking it). x/y place it at a viewport position.

menuId.description: Menu to open; defaults to the current view's photo menu.

x.description: Viewport x position in CSS pixels.

y.description: Viewport y position in CSS pixels.

examples.description: Open the photo menu for the active photo.
Open the grid photo menu at a point.

actions.availability: Available only when the library contains photos.

actions.title: Export Action Manifest
actions.description: Download the action manifest generated from the live registry: actions.json (machine-readable, with JSON Schemas) or SKILL.md (a readable guide for people and AI agents).

format.description: json for actions.json, skill for SKILL.md.

actions.title: Close Command Palette
actions.description: Close the command palette without running anything.
actions.availability: Available only when the command palette is open.

actions.title: Toggle Command Palette
actions.description: Open the command palette, a searchable list of every available action. Pass actionId to open it directly on that action's parameter form. Running it while the palette is open (with no actionId) closes it.

actionId.description: Open straight to this action's parameter step.

examples.description: Open the palette to search all actions.
Ask the user which rating to apply.

actions.title: Assign Shortcut
actions.description: Bind a key combo to an action, optionally with fixed params. Adds a new binding, or replaces the keys of binding number `replaceIndex`. Keys use `mod` for Cmd/Ctrl and spaces for chords. Saved as a user override.

keys.description: Key combo, e.g. "mod+shift+e" or "g d" (a chord).

params.description: Fixed params to dispatch with this binding.

replaceIndex.description: Replace the keys of this existing binding instead of adding one.

examples.description: Also open the grid with Shift+G.
Use Mod+Y for redo instead of the default.

actions.title: Close Keyboard Shortcuts
actions.description: Close the Keyboard Shortcuts screen.
actions.availability: Available only when the Keyboard Shortcuts screen is open.

actions.title: Export Shortcuts
actions.description: Download the user's custom shortcut overrides as a JSON file that can be imported elsewhere.

actions.title: Import Shortcuts
actions.description: Replace all custom shortcut overrides with ones from an exported JSON document. Bindings for actions that no longer exist are skipped.

json.description: Contents of a file made by Export Shortcuts.

actions.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
actions.description: Open the Keyboard Shortcuts screen, where the user can search actions, rebind keys, resolve conflicts, reset to defaults and import or export bindings as JSON.

actions.title: Reset Shortcuts
actions.description: Restore default shortcuts for one action, or for every action when actionId is omitted.

actionId.description: Reset only this action. Omit to reset all shortcuts.

examples.description: Reset every shortcut to its default.

actions.title: Remove Shortcut
actions.description: Remove binding number `index` from an action's shortcut list (see the shortcut list for indexes).

actionId.description: The action whose binding to remove.

index.description: Position of the binding in the action's list, starting at 0.

actions.title: Set Theme
actions.description: Choose the colour theme: light, dark, or follow the operating system setting. The choice is remembered.

actions.title: Toggle Light/Dark Theme
actions.description: Switch between the light and dark themes, starting from whichever one is currently showing.

actions.title: Toggle Before/After
actions.description: In Develop, switch between showing the edited photo and the original, to compare the effect of edits.
actions.availability: Available only when the current view is Develop.

actions.title: Resize Filmstrip
actions.description: Set the height of the filmstrip below the photo in Loupe and Develop, in pixels (56–360). Omit the height to restore the default.

height.description: Filmstrip height in px. Omit for the default height.

actions.title: Toggle Filmstrip
actions.description: Show or hide the strip of thumbnails below the photo in Loupe and Develop.

actions.title: Set Grid Thumbnail Size
actions.description: Set how big the thumbnails in Grid are: the target cell width in pixels (96–480); the grid fits as many columns of that width as it can. Omit the width to restore the default. The choice is remembered.

width.description: Thumbnail cell width in px. Omit for the default size.

examples.description: Big thumbnails, a few per row.

actions.title: Grid Thumbnails Larger / Smaller
actions.description: Make the Grid thumbnails one step (24px) larger or smaller. Stops at the limits (96–480px).
actions.availability: Available only when the current view is Grid.

actions.title: Toggle Info Overlay
actions.description: Show or hide capture details (camera, lens, exposure, time) over the photo in Loupe and Develop.
actions.availability: Available only when the current view is Loupe or Develop.

actions.title: Dock Develop Panel
actions.description: Attach the floating Develop controls panel back to a window edge: the given side, or the side it was last docked to.

side.description: Edge to dock to. Omit to use the previous side.

examples.description: Dock the panel where it was.
Dock the panel on the left.

actions.title: Dock / Undock Develop Panel
actions.description: Float the Develop controls panel if it is docked, or dock it back to its side if it is floating.

actions.title: Resize Develop Panel
actions.description: Set the width of the docked Develop controls panel in pixels (220–640). Omit the width to restore the default.

width.description: Panel width in px. Omit for the default width.

actions.title: Move Develop Panel to Side
actions.description: Dock the Develop controls panel to the left or right edge of the window. If the panel is floating, this docks it. The choice is remembered.

side.description: Window edge to dock the panel to.

examples.description: Put the Develop panel on the left.

actions.title: Move Develop Panel to Other Side
actions.description: Swap the Develop controls panel between the left and right edges of the window (docking it first if it is floating).

actions.title: Undock Develop Panel
actions.description: Detach the Develop controls panel so it floats over the photo and can be dragged anywhere. Optionally say where to put it (viewport pixels). Dock it again with view.panel.dock.

x.description: Left edge of the floating panel, px from the window's left.

y.description: Top edge of the floating panel, px from the window's top.

examples.description: Float the panel where it last floated.
Float the panel near the top-left corner.

actions.title: Switch View
actions.description: Switch the main view: grid (thumbnails for scanning and multi-select), loupe (the active photo, large, for close review), or develop (the active photo with editing controls).

examples.description: Review the active photo at a large size.

actions.title: Toggle Zoom
actions.description: In Loupe, switch between fitting the whole photo in the window and 100% (actual pixels) to check focus.
actions.availability: Available only when the current view is Loupe and a photo is active.

actions.title: First Photo
actions.description: Make the first visible photo active and select only it.
actions.availability: Available only when the library contains photos.

actions.title: Last Photo
actions.description: Make the last visible photo active and select only it.
actions.availability: Available only when the library contains photos.

actions.title: Next Photo
actions.description: Make the next visible photo active and select only it. Stays on the last photo at the end.
actions.availability: Available only when the library contains photos.

actions.title: Previous Photo
actions.description: Make the previous visible photo active and select only it. Stays on the first photo at the start.
actions.availability: Available only when the library contains photos.

actions.title: Set Color Label
actions.description: Apply a colour label to the selected photos (or specific photos by id). Use none to remove it.

photoIds.description: Photos to change (their ids are relative paths). Omit to use the current selection.

advance.description: Move to the next photo afterwards. When omitted, follows the auto-advance setting for interactive use; AI and scripts never advance unless this is true.

examples.description: Remove the label from one photo.

actions.availability: Available only when at least one photo is selected.

actions.title: Toggle Color Label
actions.description: Lightroom-style label key: apply the label to the selected photos, or remove it if the active photo already has that label.

advance.description: Move to the next photo afterwards. When omitted, follows the auto-advance setting for interactive use; AI and scripts never advance unless this is true.

actions.availability: Available only when at least one photo is selected.

actions.title: Clear Filter
actions.description: Remove every filter (rating, flags, labels, text) so all photos in the folder are shown again.

actions.title: Filter Photos
actions.description: Change which photos are shown. Given fields replace the current ones; omitted fields keep their value. Flags and colour labels match any of the listed values; an empty list means any.

minRating.description: Show photos rated at least this; 0 for any.

flags.description: Show only these flags; [] for any.

colorLabels.description: Show only these labels; [] for any.

text.description: Show only paths containing this text; empty for any.

actions.title: Set Flag
actions.description: Flag the selected photos (or specific photos by id) as pick, reject, or none to clear the flag.

flag.description: pick keeps, reject discards, none clears.

photoIds.description: Photos to change (their ids are relative paths). Omit to use the current selection.

advance.description: Move to the next photo afterwards. When omitted, follows the auto-advance setting for interactive use; AI and scripts never advance unless this is true.

actions.availability: Available only when at least one photo is selected.

actions.title: Open Folder…
actions.description: Ask the user to choose a folder of photos and load it, replacing the current library. Subfolders are included. Ratings, flags and labels are restored from app storage and XMP sidecars.

actions.title: Open Recent Folder
actions.description: Reopen a previously used folder by id (see library.folders.recent). May ask the user for permission.

actions.title: Reconnect Folder
actions.description: Grant the browser permission to read the last-used folder again and reload it. Needed after a restart when the browser asks for permission again.
actions.availability: Available only when the last folder needs permission to be reopened.

actions.title: List Recent Folders
actions.description: Return remembered folders (id, name, kind, whether sidecars can be written), most recent first.

actions.title: Set RAW+JPEG Grouping
actions.description: Choose how a RAW and a JPEG with the same name are treated. Grouped (the default, as in Lightroom): they are one photo; the RAW is listed, marked +JPG, and the JPEG moves with it when it is removed. Separate: they are two photos, rated and removed independently. The choice is remembered.

grouped.description: true to group each pair as one photo; false to list the RAW and the JPEG separately.

examples.description: List RAW and JPEG files separately.
Treat each RAW+JPEG pair as one photo.

actions.title: Toggle RAW+JPEG Grouping
actions.description: Switch between showing each RAW+JPEG pair as one photo (the JPEG hidden, removed with the RAW) and as two separate photos.

actions.title: List Photos
actions.description: Return photos in display order with their metadata, filtered by any combination of rating range, flags, colour labels, capture-time range (camera local time) and path text. Independent of the on-screen filter unless onlyVisible is true. Use it to find photos before acting on them by id.

minRating.description: Only photos rated at least this.

maxRating.description: Only photos rated at most this.

flags.description: Only photos with one of these flags.

colorLabels.description: Only photos with one of these labels.

capturedAfter.description: Only photos captured at or after this local time.

capturedBefore.description: Only photos captured before this local time.

text.description: Only photos whose path contains this text (case-insensitive).

onlyVisible.description: Start from the photos the on-screen filter shows.

limit.description: Return at most this many photos.

examples.description: 4+ star photos from the morning of 12 September.

actions.title: View Photos
actions.description: Look at photos as images (for the AI): returns JPEGs of the given photos, with their current develop edits applied unless original is true. Use thumbnail size to scan many photos (duplicates, obvious blur, subjects), preview to judge a look or colour, detail to check focus. Viewing costs tokens: look only at what the request needs. At most 24 thumbnails, 8 previews or 3 detail images per call.

photoIds.description: Photos to look at (ids from library.photos.list or the selection).

original.description: Show the unedited photo instead of the current edit.

examples.description: Look at one photo as currently edited.
Compare a burst for the sharpest frame.

actions.title: Set Rating
actions.description: Set the star rating (0 = unrated, 1–5 stars) on the selected photos, or on specific photos by id.

photoIds.description: Photos to change (their ids are relative paths). Omit to use the current selection.

advance.description: Move to the next photo afterwards. When omitted, follows the auto-advance setting for interactive use; AI and scripts never advance unless this is true.

examples.description: Clear the rating of one specific photo.

actions.availability: Available only when at least one photo is selected.

actions.title: Remove Rejected Photos
actions.description: Move rejected photos (and their XMP sidecars) out of the library into the folder's _Rejected subfolder. Nothing is deleted: undo, or Restore Removed Photos, brings them back until that folder is emptied. Defaults to every rejected photo; photoIds limits it to some of them.

photoIds.description: Only these rejected photos. Omit for all rejected photos.

examples.description: Move every rejected photo to the _Rejected folder.

actions.availability: Available only when the folder was opened with write access and at least one photo is flagged rejected.

actions.title: Delete Removed Photos Permanently
actions.description: Permanently delete everything in the _Rejected subfolder. This cannot be undone and the files do not go to the system Trash, and it clears undo history. Requires confirm: true; always ask the user first.

confirm.description: Must be true: confirms the user agreed to delete the files permanently.

examples.description: After the user confirms, delete the removed photos for good.

actions.availability: Available only when the folder was opened with write access and the folder's _Rejected subfolder contains removed photos.

actions.title: List Removed Photos
actions.description: Return photos in the _Rejected subfolder by their original path, with size and modified time.

actions.title: Restore Removed Photos
actions.description: Move photos back from the _Rejected subfolder to where they were, with their ratings and sidecars. Defaults to all of them. Undoable.

photoIds.description: Original paths to restore (see List Removed Photos). Omit for all.

actions.availability: Available only when the folder was opened with write access and the folder's _Rejected subfolder contains removed photos.

actions.title: Open Sample Library
actions.description: Load the built-in sample library of placeholder photos, for trying the app without real files.

actions.title: Select All
actions.description: Select every photo that passes the current filter, keeping the active photo if it is visible.
actions.availability: Available only when the library contains photos.

actions.title: Get Selection
actions.description: Return the active photo id and the selected photos with their metadata (rating, flag, label, capture time, EXIF).

actions.title: Select Photos
actions.description: Replace the selection with the given photos. activeId (default: the first id) becomes the active photo shown in Loupe and Develop.

ids.description: Photo ids to select, in order.

activeId.description: Which selected photo becomes active. Must be in ids.

examples.description: Select three, with the middle one active.

actions.availability: Available only when the library contains photos.

actions.title: Sort Photos
actions.description: Choose the display order: capture time, file name, rating or file size, ascending or descending.

actions.title: Adjust Setting
actions.description: Set (value) or nudge (delta) one slider on the selected photos: temperature, tint, exposure (stops, -5 to 5), contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, vibrance, saturation or vignette (-100 to 100; negative vignette darkens the corners, positive lightens them). Use delta to change each photo relative to its current setting.

value.description: New value (clamped to the slider's range).

delta.description: Amount to add to the current value.

photoIds.description: Photos to change. Omit to use the current selection.

examples.description: Brighten the selection by a third of a stop.

actions.availability: Available only when at least one photo is selected.

actions.title: Auto Tone
actions.description: Automatically set the selected photos' tone (exposure, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, vibrance) and/or white balance (temperature, tint) from each photo's own pixels, inside its crop. Each photo is analysed separately and the result accounts for its profile and other settings, so apply a profile first. Tone replaces those sliders; nothing else changes. One undo step for all photos.

include.description: What to set: tone, wb (white balance), or both. Defaults to tone.

photoIds.description: Photos to change. Omit to use the current selection.

examples.description: Both, for a batch of photos straight off the card.

actions.availability: Available only when at least one photo is selected.

actions.title: Straighten Along Line
actions.description: Straighten the active photo so a line along a horizon or vertical edge becomes level (horizontal, or vertical when the line is closer to vertical). from/to are fractions (0–1, y down) of the uncropped photo as currently straightened; with no straighten angle yet, that is the original photo. The crop is kept inside the rotated photo.

examples.description: Level a horizon that rises to the right.

actions.availability: Available only when a photo is active.

actions.title: Crop & Straighten
actions.description: Set the crop rectangle (fractions of the straightened photo: x, y, width, height) and/or straighten angle (-45 to 45 degrees) on the selected photos. The crop is kept inside the rotated photo automatically. Use aspect to crop to a ratio, as large as fits.

aspect.description: Crop to this aspect ratio (width:height), centred and as large as fits.

photoIds.description: Photos to change. Omit to use the current selection.

actions.availability: Available only when at least one photo is selected.

actions.title: Crop Tool
actions.description: Show or hide the crop & straighten overlay on the active photo in Loupe or Develop, where the crop can be moved, resized and rotated.
actions.availability: Available only when the current view is Loupe or Develop and a photo is active.

actions.title: Export JPEG
actions.description: Render the selected photos with their edits at full resolution (or limited to maxEdge pixels on the long side) and save them as JPEGs: into the folder's _Exports subfolder when it is writable, otherwise as downloads. Originals are untouched; existing exports are never overwritten.

maxEdge.description: Longest side in pixels; omit for full size.

destination.description: folder (_Exports) or download; defaults to folder when writable.

photoIds.description: Photos to change. Omit to use the current selection.

examples.description: Export the selection at full size.

actions.availability: Available only when at least one photo is selected.

actions.title: Set HSL
actions.description: Adjust one colour band's hue, saturation or luminance (-100 to 100) on the selected photos. Bands: red, orange, yellow, green, aqua, blue, purple, magenta. E.g. lower blue luminance to darken a sky.

photoIds.description: Photos to change. Omit to use the current selection.

actions.availability: Available only when at least one photo is selected.

actions.title: Straighten Tool
actions.description: Arm or disarm the straighten tool in Loupe or Develop: the next drag over the photo draws a line along a horizon or vertical edge, and the photo is rotated to make it level. Opens the crop overlay. (In the crop overlay, ⌘/Ctrl-drag does the same without arming it.)

on.description: Arm (true) or disarm (false); omit to toggle.

actions.availability: Available only when the current view is Loupe or Develop and a photo is active.

actions.title: Set Profile
actions.description: Apply a profile (a film look under the sliders: colour or black and white, curves, toning, grain) to the selected photos, or "none" to remove it. The sliders are kept. amount is its strength in percent (0–200, default 100); amount alone changes the strength of each photo's current profile. Ids come from develop.profiles.list.

profileId.description: Profile id from develop.profiles.list, or "none" to remove the profile.

amount.description: Strength in percent, 0–200 (100 is the profile as designed).

photoIds.description: Photos to change. Omit to use the current selection.

actions.availability: Available only when at least one photo is selected.

actions.title: New Profile
actions.description: Create one of the user's own profiles. It starts from another profile's look (from), else the active photo's current profile, else neutral; look then changes any fields. Returns the new id. Use develop.profile.set to apply it.

name.description: Name shown in the profile browser.

curves.description: Channel curves to replace (red, green, blue): control points [input, output] in 0–1.

monochrome.description: Black and white channel mix in percent (red, green, blue), or null to make the look colour.

splitToning.description: Split toning fields to change: hues in degrees, saturations 0–100, balance -100 to 100.

look.description: Look fields to change; anything omitted is kept.

examples.description: A more faded copy of Sepia.

actions.title: Delete Profile
actions.description: Delete one of the user's own profiles. Photos that use it keep their look (each edit holds a copy of it). Undoable. Built-in profiles can't be deleted.

actions.title: Export Profiles
actions.description: Save profiles to a JSON file on the user's disk (a download) to back them up or share them; develop.profiles.import loads them back. Exports the given ids (built-in or the user's own), or all of the user's own profiles.

ids.description: Profiles to export. Omit for all of your own.

actions.availability: Available only when there are profiles to export.

actions.title: Get Profile
actions.description: Return one profile's full definition (name, description, look), built-in or the user's own.

actions.title: Import Profiles
actions.description: Add the profiles in a profiles file (the parsed JSON written by develop.profiles.export) to the user's own. A profile identical to an existing one is skipped; one whose id is already used is added as a copy with a new name, unless replace is true, which overwrites it (and updates photos here that use it).

curves.description: Red, green and blue curves: control points [input, output] in 0–1.

monochrome.description: Black and white channel mix in percent (e.g. 30/59/11 neutral, high red darkens skies); null for colour.

saturation.description: Overall saturation of the look, -100 to 100.

fade.description: Lifts the blacks for a faded print, 0 to 100.

splitToning.description: Tints shadows and highlights: hues in degrees, saturation 0 to 100, balance -100 (shadows) to 100 (highlights).

grain.description: Film grain: amount 0 to 100, size 0 (fine) to 100 (coarse).

profiles.description: Profiles: name, optional id and description, and look.

file.description: The contents of a profiles file (as exported).

replace.description: Overwrite your profiles that have the same id instead of adding copies.

actions.title: List Profiles
actions.description: List the available profiles: built-in film looks and the user's own, with id, name, group (color or bw), description, and how many photos in this folder use each. Pass includeLooks for their full settings.

includeLooks.description: Include each profile's look (curves, toning, grain…).

actions.title: Edit Profile
actions.description: Change one of the user's own profiles: rename it, change its description, or change look fields. Photos in this folder that use it are updated too (photos elsewhere keep the look they were given until it is applied again). Built-in profiles can't be changed.

curves.description: Channel curves to replace (red, green, blue): control points [input, output] in 0–1.

monochrome.description: Black and white channel mix in percent (red, green, blue), or null to make the look colour.

splitToning.description: Split toning fields to change: hues in degrees, saturations 0–100, balance -100 to 100.

look.description: Look fields to change; anything omitted is kept.

actions.title: Reset Develop Settings
actions.description: Reset the selected photos' develop settings to unedited, or only the given groups.

groups.description: Only these groups (profile, wb, basic, presence, effects, toneCurve, hsl, crop). Omit for all.

photoIds.description: Photos to change. Omit to use the current selection.

actions.availability: Available only when at least one photo is selected.

actions.title: Apply Develop Settings
actions.description: Apply several develop settings at once to the selected photos (a look or preset): any Basic sliders, tone curve, HSL bands, crop. Values replace the current ones; omitted settings are unchanged.

hsl.description: Per-colour adjustments, -100 to 100, by band (red, orange, yellow, green, aqua, blue, purple, magenta).

settings.description: Settings to change; anything omitted is left as it is.

photoIds.description: Photos to change. Omit to use the current selection.

actions.availability: Available only when at least one photo is selected.

actions.title: Copy Settings
actions.description: Copy the active photo's develop settings (by default everything except crop) to paste onto other photos.

groups.description: Settings groups: profile, wb, basic, presence, effects, toneCurve, hsl, crop. Defaults to everything except crop.

examples.description: Copy only white balance and the curve.

actions.availability: Available only when a photo is active.

actions.title: Get Develop Settings
actions.description: Return a photo's full develop settings (the active photo by default) and whether it has been edited.

actions.title: Paste Settings
actions.description: Paste copied develop settings onto the selected photos (only the groups that were copied).

photoIds.description: Photos to change. Omit to use the current selection.

actions.availability: Available only when at least one photo is selected and develop settings have been copied.

actions.title: Sync Settings
actions.description: Copy the active photo's develop settings to every other selected photo (by default everything except crop).

groups.description: Settings groups: profile, wb, basic, presence, effects, toneCurve, hsl, crop. Defaults to everything except crop.

actions.availability: Available only when a photo is active and more than one photo is selected.

actions.title: Set Tone Curve
actions.description: Replace the master tone curve on the selected photos with control points [input, output] in 0–1. [[0,0],[1,1]] is neutral; lifting the first point fades blacks, an S-shape adds contrast.

photoIds.description: Photos to change. Omit to use the current selection.

examples.description: Faded film look: lifted blacks, softer whites.

actions.availability: Available only when at least one photo is selected.

actions.title: Redo
actions.description: Redo the most recently undone change.
actions.availability: Available only when there is an undone action to redo.

actions.title: Undo
actions.description: Undo the most recent undoable change. A transaction (such as an applied AI plan) is undone as one step.
actions.availability: Available only when there is an action to undo.

menus.title: Photo
menus.description: Right-click on a photo in the grid or filmstrip. Acts on the selection (the clicked photo is selected first).

menus.title: Photo
menus.description: Right-click on the photo in Loupe or Develop.
